plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful ornamental cherry tree that produces clouds of pale pink-white, five-petaled flowers on bare branches before the leaves emerge. It is the iconic tree of hanami (flower viewing) festivals and is widely planted in parks and along rivers and avenues.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in Japan; blooms in warmer regions such as southern Japan and parts of the southern US from early to mid-March
plants.location: Japan (Kyushu and southern Honshu), Washington D.C. region, Korea, and temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: The first cherry trees in Washington D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and the National Cherry Blossom Festival commemorates this gift every spring.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals and blue-green strap-like leaves. It naturalizes in woodlands, meadows, and grassy banks, and countless cultivars are grown in gardens.
plants.location: Western Europe (UK, France, Spain, Belgium), naturalized in North America and temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain the alkaloid galantamine, which is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease, and the plants are toxic to many grazing animals, so they are rarely eaten.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A majestic deciduous tree bearing enormous, goblet-shaped flowers up to 30 cm across on bare branches. The blossoms open in dramatic displays of pink and rose-magenta and can appear spectacular in mild, humid climates.
plants.location: Himalayan foothills (Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, southwestern China); cultivated in mild gardens in Cornwall, Ireland, New Zealand, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Magnolia campbellii may take 20 to 30 years from seed before it flowers for the first time, and magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, having evolved before bees existed and being pollinated by beetles.

plants.name: Amaryllis belladonna
plants.description: A bulbous perennial in which strong, bare flower stalks emerge without leaves, topped by clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers. The strap-like leaves appear later in the season after flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn in the Southern Hemisphere (February to April)
plants.location: Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, New Zealand, Chile, and California
plants.funFact: Its nickname 'Naked Lady' comes from the way the flower stalks rise out of the bare ground with no leaves, and the plant is a classic autumn bloomer in the Southern Hemisphere when March is early fall.
